p: For a lot of people, Britannia Pier means one thing: a night at the theatre. The pavilion stage has hosted comedians, tribute acts, pantomimes and summer variety shows for decades, and catching a performance here is one of those classic seaside traditions that still feels special. Arrive a little early, grab a bite on the seafront and stroll down the boards as the sun sets for the full experience.

During the day, the pier is a cracking place to stretch your legs and get a bit of sea air. Wander to the end, lean on the railings and watch the waves roll in below, or turn back for one of the best views of Great Yarmouth's seafront, with the beach, the prom and the bright frontages of Marine Parade lined up before you. Gulls will be keeping a beady eye on any chips, so guard them carefully.

Families will find plenty to keep kids happy, from rides to sweet treats, and there's something about being out over the water that makes even a simple doughnut taste better. Some of the pier's amusements are family arcades, and if you spot any adults-only areas along the seafront, they're 18+ and for grown-ups only.

Britannia Pier sits close to the northern end of the main seafront, handy for a couple of Great Yarmouth's best-loved spots. The Venetian Waterways, a restored 1920s boating lake and gardens, are a short walk north and a lovely place for a gentle paddle-boat trip. Head south along the prom and you'll pass Sea Life and the bustle of the Golden Mile on the way to Wellington Pier, Great Yarmouth's other historic pier, and the Pleasure Beach beyond.
